The carving of the Indian epic Ramayana in stone reliefs on the Hindu temples of Prambanan in central Java, in the mid 9th century. It is one of the clearest signs of how Indian stories were taken up in Southeast Asia and made local.

Prambanan was built by the kings of Mataram and dedicated to the Hindu trinity of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. The Ramayana panels run around the balustrades of the Shiva and Brahma temples, so pilgrims read the story as they walked clockwise around them. The Vishnu temple carries scenes from the life of Krishna. The figures, plants and houses in the panels are Javanese, not Indian.

The same story was written in Old Javanese verse about the same time in the Kakawin Ramayana. Nearby stands the Buddhist Borobudur, built a few decades earlier, so both faiths raised great monuments side by side. Since 1961 a Ramayana dance drama has been staged at Prambanan on full moon nights.
